# git C-quotes paths with non-ASCII bytes in its --name-only output
# (".sesam/objects/h\303\251llo.txt.sesam"). A quoted path matches no real file,
# so the finalize used to skip it: the revealed plaintext stayed stale and the
# seal wrote it back over the incoming object - a silent revert that `verify`
# and `status` both called clean.

sesam-repo admin base.txt changed.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt héllo.txt
exec sesam add héllo.txt --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secret with a non-ascii name'

# THEIRS changes the secret, OURS only adds another one - so no object is
# touched twice and git resolves both sides without calling the driver.
exec git checkout -b topic
cp $TMPDIR/changed.txt héllo.txt
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change it'

exec git checkout master
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt other.txt
exec sesam add other.txt --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'master: add other'

! exec git merge topic -m merged
exec git commit --no-edit

# Theirs' change survives in both the plaintext and the object.
exec cat héllo.txt
stdout 'CHANGED'
exec sesam show '.sesam/objects/héllo.txt.sesam'
stdout 'CHANGED'

exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'
exec sesam status
stdout 'in sync'
! stdout 'out of sync'

-- base.txt --
line one
BASE
line three
-- changed.txt --
line one
CHANGED
line three
